name: Tonga (Zambia)
notes: Standard Chitonga (Zambian Tonga) Latin orthography as harmonized by Zambia's Ministry of Education in 1977 alongside Bemba, Nyanja, Lozi, Kaonde, Luvale and Lunda (the seven official Zambian regional languages); the earlier standard grammar is Collins (1962), A Shona-Tonga-English Vocabulary, and Carter & Kahari's Tonga language materials. Five-vowel system /a e i o u/. ⟨c⟩ and ⟨j⟩ spell the single (retroflex-shifted) affricates /t̠ʃ/ and /d̠ʒ/ (not c+h or a stop-glide sequence). Prenasalized series ⟨mb⟩ /mb/, ⟨mp⟩ /mp/, ⟨nd⟩ /nd/, ⟨nt⟩ /nt/, ⟨ns⟩ /ns/, ⟨nz⟩ /nz/, ⟨nc⟩ /n̠t̠ʃ/, ⟨nj⟩ /n̠d̠ʒ/, ⟨nsh⟩ /n̠ʃ/, ⟨mf⟩ /ɱf/, ⟨mv⟩ /ɱv/, ⟨ng⟩ /ŋɡ/ and ⟨nk⟩ /ŋk/ each spell one prenasalized segment, not a nasal followed by an oral obstruent (AGENTS.md test 2, the same pattern documented for Tiv). ⟨ng'⟩ (with a following apostrophe) spells the plain velar nasal /ŋ/, distinguishing it from the prenasalized-stop ⟨ng⟩ sequence: the apostrophe blocks the wrong maximal-munch match onto the /ŋɡ/ digraph (AGENTS.md test 3). ⟨ny⟩ is the palatal nasal /ɲ/, ⟨sh⟩ /ʃ/. Intervocalic ⟨b⟩ has a fricative allophone [β] and ⟨l⟩ a flapped allophone [ɾ] (both cited in the PHOIBLE-sourced inventory). Smoke-tested against the cited Wikipedia example pair distinguishing tone by minimal pair: ⟨íbúsi⟩ 'smoke' vs ⟨ibusu⟩ 'flour' — both resolve through the same segmental graphemes (i-b-u-s-i/u), differing only in the tone diacritic this spec does not encode, and ⟨kutonga⟩-type infinitive ku- forms shared across the Bantu Zambian language cluster (e.g. Luvale ⟨kutonga⟩ 'to sew') confirm the ku- infinitive prefix segments (k-u) map correctly. Tonga is a two-tone (high/low) Bantu (M64) language with grammatical tone movement (e.g. the íbúsi/ibusu pair) rather than lexical stress; tone is not consistently marked in ordinary orthography and is left unencoded here, a documented exemption distinct from stress (docs/quality_tiers.md).
